markdown_report:
The best first experiment remains **terminal-aligned mixed masking within the supplied BERT4Rec**, using one network per category. Revise the proposal to specify loss weighting and distinguish inference alignment from recency. No improvement is established before validation.

**Insights from the starting point.** First, interior reconstruction can use future context unavailable during appended-mask inference. Second, users report stale interests and broad matches displacing specific choices; next-choice supervision addresses the latter directly, while benefits for current priorities remain hypothetical. Third, Industrial_and_Scientific and Electronics have wrong-rank rates of 12.25% and 11.27%. Fourth, embedding scores near 0.5 indicate near-zero mean cosine similarity, not widespread collapse.

**Insights from related work.** [BERT4Rec](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06690) already proposes terminal training; its [public implementation](https://github.com/FeiSun/BERT4Rec) differs in sampling and loss reduction. [Recency Sampling](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.02643) favors newer targets, whereas uniform-prefix sampling does not. [Sampled Softmax](https://wujcan.github.io/papers/tois-ssm.pdf) motivates a separate objective experiment. [Semantic Fusion](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.18166) supports contextual content integration, without establishing compatibility.

The framework retains three directions:

| Direction | Intervention | Diagnostic target | Main uncertainty |
|---|---|---|---|
| Prediction alignment | Prefix-terminal masking | Specific next choices; weak margins | Sampling and context-length effects |
| Candidate discrimination | Uniform sampled softmax | Broad matches; wrong ranks | False negatives and temperature |
| Content specificity | Joint title/description gate | Fine distinctions | Sparse text; compatibility ambiguity |

Scores are hypotheses; difficulty 10 means hardest. Each cell states a benefit and limitation.

| Idea | Originality | Potential | User alignment | Model alignment | Difficulty |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mixed prefix-terminal masking | 2: controlled refinement / established | 6: reusable / modest novelty | 6: next choices / current intent latent | 7: aligned separation / uncertain transfer | 4: small change / weighting and probes |
| Uniform sampled softmax | 3: grounded / established | 7: scalable / tuning sensitive | 5: discrimination / weak specificity | 8: separation / false negatives | 4: shared candidates / exclusions |
| Gated text–ID embeddings | 5: useful combination / precedented | 7: richer inputs / sparse metadata | 8: finer distinctions / no ownership evidence | 6: richer features / uncertain gains | 6: joint encoder / predictor changes |

Select mixed prefix-terminal masking at 0% progress. Sample users uniformly and eligible prefix endpoints uniformly within users. Split each batch equally between terminal and interior examples; average losses within examples, then within branches, and combine branches equally. This explicitly changes sampling and reduction; retain the baseline target loss. Preserve corrected interior corruption, documenting its exact eligibility, rounding and caps before execution.

The proposal targets stale-interest emphasis and broad relevance displacing specific choices, but uniform endpoints provide no explicit recency weighting. Its measurable model target is weak separation. Freeze training-only interior and terminal probe panels, and report them separately. Keep unknown-item skips unassessable.

Compare with the supplied baseline using unchanged macro validation HR@10, equal validation schedules and recorded GPU-seconds, updates and target counts. [Sampled metrics](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/) do not establish full-catalog superiority. Paired, category-stratified user bootstraps are descriptive after checkpoint selection; record every validation query to expose [selection overfitting](https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v11/cawley10a.html).

idea.description: Train one corrected BERT4Rec per category with equally weighted terminal-prefix and interior-mask branches. Uniformly sample a training-only target endpoint for terminal examples, remove that target and every later interaction, and append the reserved mask. Make branch weighting explicit through per-example loss reduction rather than assuming that equal example counts imply equal objective weights.
idea.motivation: Terminal examples reproduce the future-context restriction and final mask position of appended-mask inference. The hypothesis addresses two user failures: broad relevance displacing specific next choices, and historical interests receiving weight without sufficient attention to current priorities. Support for the second connection is weaker: uniform endpoints are not recency sampling and cannot reveal present intent. The model-facing target is weak positive–negative separation, especially the negative margin tails in Industrial_and_Scientific and Electronics. Neither compatibility, ownership nor mood is directly observed, and no gains are established.
idea.implementation_notes:
Preserve all four categories, routing, the supplied bidirectional BERT4Rec backbone, optimizer settings initially, checkpoint format and predictor writer. Train exactly one independent network per category and load exactly one selected checkpoint per category; do not average checkpoints or combine separately fitted scores. Keep DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, at most 200 epochs and exactly 200 batches per epoch. All attempts and diagnostics count against 43,200 GPU-seconds. No baseline source was supplied in this prompt, so the code is an integration helper, not a standalone replacement train.py.

Sample eligible users uniformly from users with at least two training interactions. For each example, draw the target index uniformly from 1 through n-1 in zero-based indexing. Terminal contexts contain at most L-1 preceding items; L includes the appended mask. This induces context-length and truncation changes and is not a recency-weighted distribution. Reserve mask_id outside real item IDs and exclude padding/mask IDs from output candidates. Preserve the baseline training-only negative sampler for this first experiment. Unobserved sampled items may still be false negatives.

Use equal branch counts in an even-sized batch. Reduce the unchanged target loss to a mean over valid supervised targets within each example, average those example means within each branch, then combine with coefficients 0.5 and 0.5. Do not globally flatten targets before reduction: with k interior targets and one terminal target, global target averaging would assign approximate coefficients k/(k+1) and 1/(k+1). If the supplied baseline uses global target averaging, this proposal changes both sampling and reduction; identify it accordingly. A reduction-only control is needed before attributing a gain exclusively to terminal sampling.

Retain the corrected baseline interior-mask constructor, including its context windows, eligible positions, replacement probabilities, target-count rounding and cap. Record their exact values from the supplied implementation before execution; these values are unavailable here and must not be invented from the original paper. Require at least one valid target per example and fail on invalid construction rather than silently changing branch weights. A terminal example must never use a shifted target visible elsewhere as its supervised position; repeated item IDs naturally present in earlier history are allowed.

Preserve ModelView.item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data and review_data. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), returning measured metrics and definitions. The loader remains (None, sequence, positive, negative), with B x L tensors. Freeze common training-only probe examples independently of training sampling. Use separate interior and terminal panels with matched users, target identities, corruption, truncation and candidates across compared models. Gather features at actual supervised positions and exclude padding and unmasked positions. Report target-level cross-entropy, margin distributions, wrong-rank rates, explicit denominators and per-user averages. Do not pool the panels because interior examples have right context. Do not infer unavailable item categories from empty breakdowns or interpret embedding scores near 0.5 as collapse.

Retain appended-mask inference and matching checkpoint/predictor architecture. For fixed-width left-padded terminal examples, the readout is features[:, -1]; a general implementation must use the maximum nonpadding index, never nonpadding_count-1. Padding tokens must remain excluded from attention and losses. Titles, descriptions and historical timestamps are the only optional content inputs; this experiment does not add them. Reviews, ratings, prices, stores, categories, simulator traits and target timestamps are unavailable. Unknown-item simulator skips remain unassessable, not negative labels.

Predeclare identical validation frequency, checkpoint-selection rule and per-configuration resource cap for baseline and proposal. Use the host rule where supplied; otherwise select maximum macro validation HR@10 with earliest-checkpoint tie breaking. Record all configurations, validation queries, GPU-seconds, optimizer updates, examples and supervised targets. Equal epochs or equal branch coefficients do not equalize target counts or compute. Do not expand the initial experiment into an uncontrolled factorial search. If resources permit, prioritize a reduction-only control, then terminal-only versus mixed training with shared endpoint draws and documented target-count accounting. Subsequent uniform-versus-recency comparisons require matched context-length strata and independently controlled context caps. Position-ID ablations must preserve tokens, padding and attention while changing position indexing consistently at training and inference.

Log target age, visible-context length, truncation rate and target-position frequencies; inspect host validation hits by training-history length if available without extra evaluator changes. Use identical pinned candidates for baseline/proposal comparisons. If host outputs expose per-user hit indicators, bootstrap paired users within each category and average category differences equally. One changed hit changes category HR@10 by 0.005 and macro HR@10 by 0.00125. Such intervals condition on candidates and checkpoints, exclude training-seed and candidate-sampling variability, and are descriptive after selection. Sampled HR@10 does not establish full-catalog quality for simulator recommendations. Never inspect hidden test files or change the evaluator.
idea.pseudocode:
import numpy as np
import torch


def terminal_masked_example(history, maxlen, mask_id, rng):
    """Only training interactions; rng is initialized by the seeded caller."""
    if maxlen < 2 or len(history) < 2:
        raise ValueError('Need context, mask, and two training interactions')
    if mask_id <= 0 or mask_id in history:
        raise ValueError('mask_id must be reserved outside real item IDs')
    # Uniform over eligible target indices, not recency-weighted.
    t = int(rng.integers(1, len(history)))
    context = np.asarray(history[max(0, t - maxlen + 1):t], dtype=np.int64)
    sequence = np.zeros(maxlen, dtype=np.int64)
    positive = np.zeros(maxlen, dtype=np.int64)
    sequence[-len(context)-1:-1] = context
    sequence[-1] = mask_id
    positive[-1] = int(history[t])
    return sequence, positive, positive != 0


def balanced_mask_loss(target_loss, positive, terminal_rows):
    """target_loss: unreduced baseline loss, shape B x L.
    positive: aligned masked-target labels, zero elsewhere.
    terminal_rows: boolean B-vector assigned by batch constructor.
    """
    valid = positive.ne(0)
    count = valid.sum(dim=1)
    if torch.any(count == 0):
        raise ValueError('Every example must contain a supervised target')
    terminal_rows = terminal_rows.to(device=positive.device, dtype=torch.bool)
    n_terminal = int(terminal_rows.sum().item())
    if n_terminal == 0 or 2 * n_terminal != positive.shape[0]:
        raise ValueError('Require equal nonempty terminal/interior branches')
    per_example = target_loss.masked_fill(~valid, 0).sum(dim=1) / count
    return (0.5 * per_example[terminal_rows].mean()
            + 0.5 * per_example[~terminal_rows].mean())


# Integration into supplied family-specific sample_batch:
# 1. Require even batch size. Assign exactly B/2 terminal rows, then shuffle rows.
# 2. Sample each eligible user uniformly using the seeded training RNG.
# 3. Terminal row: use terminal_masked_example(training_history, L, mask_id, rng).
# 4. Interior row: retain corrected baseline interior constructor unchanged.
#    Record its eligibility, mask count rounding/cap, and replacement rules.
#    Require positive != 0 exactly at supervised positions and >=1 target.
# 5. Generate negatives with the supplied training-only sampler.
# 6. Return (None, sequence, positive, negative), tensors B x L;
#    retain the row-type vector as training metadata for loss reduction.
# 7. Compute baseline target loss with reduction='none', then balanced_mask_loss.
# 8. Preserve one model/checkpoint per category and appended-mask inference.
#    For the terminal sequences constructed above: features[:, -1].
# 9. Run frozen, training-only interior and terminal diagnostic panels separately.
#    Compare fixed host validation hits; do not modify evaluator or read test labels.

originality.positive: Explicit branch normalization and controlled prefix sampling make a useful, reproducible refinement of BERT4Rec training.
originality.negative: Terminal masking is already proposed by BERT4Rec; neither the objective nor uniform prefix sampling supports a strong novelty claim.

future_potential.positive: A small initial experiment can establish whether inference alignment merits further investment before adding content encoders or hard-negative mining.
future_potential.negative: Sampling, context lengths, positional supervision and loss reduction can confound the result; missing compatibility evidence and sampled evaluation limit broader conclusions.

code_difficulty.positive: The architecture and checkpoint format remain unchanged, and the principal training changes are example construction and loss reduction.
code_difficulty.negative: Exact branch weighting, baseline corruption documentation, frozen family-specific probes and compute accounting require more integration than a sampler-only change.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec: Sequential Recommendation with Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer
contributions: Introduces bidirectional masked-item sequential recommendation and appended-mask next-item inference.
Section 3.6 proposes additional last-item-only training examples.
Equation 8 averages masked-target cross-entropy within an example.
limitations: Does not specify or validate the proposed 50:50 branch weighting or uniform-prefix endpoint distribution.
Does not isolate effects of this task's fixed-width left padding.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec public implementation: data generator and loss
contributions: gen_data.py constructs history windows and random-mask variants, selecting positions uniformly without replacement.
The published training generator uses force_last=False; evaluation uses force_last=True.
run.py reduces cross-entropy over total valid target weight, producing per-target batch averaging.
limitations: The implementation does not explicitly instantiate the paper's additional terminal-training mixture.
Its defaults must not be assumed to match the host's corrected baseline.
Equal terminal/interior example counts do not yield equal loss coefficients under per-target batch averaging.

related_work.title: Recency Sampling
contributions: Motivates target sampling that assigns greater probability to newer interactions.
limitations: Uniform-prefix terminal sampling is inference alignment rather than explicit recency sampling.
Experiments on GRU4Rec, Caser and SASRec do not establish gains for this BERT4Rec modification.

related_work.title: Sampled Softmax for Item Recommendation
contributions: Studies efficient shared negative sampling and temperature sensitivity.
limitations: Does not establish improvements for the corrected BERT4Rec benchmark.
Unobserved sampled items may be false negatives; aggressive temperatures can overemphasize difficult candidates.

related_work.title: Sequence-level Semantic Representation Fusion
contributions: Motivates contextual integration of semantic and item-ID representations.
limitations: Does not establish that a randomly initialized lightweight text encoder improves this benchmark.
Semantic similarity cannot establish equipment compatibility, ownership or present need.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled recommendation metrics can yield different model rankings from full-catalog metrics.
limitations: Does not invalidate the mandated benchmark or justify changing its candidates.
Does not establish full-catalog superiority from a gain on the pinned sampled HR@10.

related_work.title: On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation
contributions: Explains how repeated model selection can overfit finite validation estimates.
limitations: Does not provide a selection-adjusted confidence interval for this adaptive search.
Paired bootstrap intervals for selected checkpoints remain descriptive without accounting for the selection process.
